# Agent Circuit Breaker (ACB)

> Open-source Python safety layer by Sagar Chhatrala. Local deterministic checks for agent actions and trajectories, plus typed local execution, durable stdio MCP, and exact approvals through a stateful RuntimeGate for trusted single-host integrations.

Reviewed version: 1.7.2 (beta), 2026-11-11.
Source revision: 7c04c3900460a633400bd1b6b5d0a5cca2df9f20.
Python: 3.11+. License: MIT. Default runtime dependencies: Python standard library only.
Install: python -m pip install agent-circuit-breaker==1.7.2
Demo: agent-circuit-breaker demo
Typed file workflows require Linux/macOS. The demo is offline and needs no API key.

## Supported capabilities

- Evaluate shell commands, filesystem operations, and SQL against supported deterministic checks.
- Explicit outcomes: ALLOW, BLOCK, UNKNOWN, PENDING_APPROVAL, ERROR. UNKNOWN is not execution authority.
- Trajectory checks use run history and configured contracts for actors, delegation, output channels, targets, blocked retries, and supported secret-to-egress patterns.
- RuntimeGate and RuntimeToolExecutor bind execution to current policy, configured principal/capability authority, action-specific approvals, and run state.
- Exact approvals and authorizations are consumed once before the executor starts.
- SQLite persists run history, suspension, revocation, execution starts, and outcomes. Unresolved execution requires explicit trusted reconciliation.
- Local audit chains, optional HMAC signatures, and independent checkpoints support evidence verification.
- CLI runtime-health, runtime-inspect, production-check, and safe-validate inspect the local runtime setup. safe-validate uses synthetic test-file side effects.

## Existing typed workflow and local demo (introduced in v1.7.0)

- Six typed tools bind reads, repository status, reports, copies, Base64 encoding, and publication to explicit owner permissions and exact artifact versions.
- Authenticated provenance retains sensitivity through supported transformations; arbitrary shell/Python/model information flow is not tracked.
- Exact owner approvals are expiring, revocable, and single-use; capability expiry is rechecked at start.
- Unresolved effects persist through restart and prevent automatic retries.
- New, removed, changed, or malformed catalog definitions quarantine until owner review. Definitions do not attest remote implementations.
- The packaged demo covers useful work, unauthorized export, exact approval, interruption, and catalog changes. Proposals are scripted offline; backend observations are fresh on each local run.
- Publishing gates build once and promote the same wheel/source archive bytes through TestPyPI and PyPI, then verify a fresh public install.

## New in v1.7.2

- Separate owner service with Unix agent/control sockets and OS peer identity. Protected mode requires distinct UIDs; same-UID development does not isolate an agent.
- Owner-registered parameterized SQLite UPDATE/DELETE, private-copy preview, exact snapshot approval, transactional revalidation, and actual row-count limits.
- S3-compatible SigV4 conditional publication, exact artifact/destination binding, SHA-256, no redirects, and no automatic retry after uncertainty.
- Cumulative created-file, affected-row, and S3 payload-byte budgets. Atomic reservations apply even after approval and persist through restart; trusted executors settle measured effects.
- Canonical JSON and pattern redaction preserve sensitivity labels. Only owner review can declassify exact bytes.
- Paginated HMAC-authenticated evidence export and independent verification.
- Thin owner MCP client and guided `--owner-socket` configuration. Existing Workflow catalog, evaluators, rule schema and unbudgeted RuntimeGate contracts remain compatible; the owner route and budgets are opt-in.

## Security fixes in v1.7.1, retained in v1.7.2

Stricter uninspectable MCP calls; path, shell-option and SQL handling; zero-limit semantics; protected-key signed run ledgers; serialized/flushed audit appends; checkpoint verification; and the installed pre-commit command. Empty/numeric-only calls need a typed adapter or an explicit reviewed empty-tool grant. Existing unsigned logs are not retroactively authenticated; archive them and start a new log when enabling a protected HMAC key.

## Integration and enforcement boundary

The owner service separates resources and authority from agent requests. Protected use requires OS isolation and removal of alternate resource access. SQLite is a bounded maintenance profile; export-byte budgets count S3 payloads, not arbitrary information flow. Pattern redaction does not declassify. Native desktop hosts and live AWS are not certified.

The supported authority model remains single-host: every protected side effect passes through RuntimeToolExecutor, execute_authorized, or execute_approved; trusted workers share one local SQLite store; private keys remain outside model-visible and attacker-writable state.

CLI and Python policy evaluation are advisory unless the caller gates execution on the results. The v1.7.2 workflow-mcp stdio server executes six typed tools through the durable Workflow dispatcher, supports modern discovery and legacy initialization, and keeps one server per state directory. The Responses dispatcher uses the same execution path and protects against call-ID replay; its offline path is tested, live API use is unverified.

The legacy MCP proxy can stop forwarding unsafe or unknown calls by policy but does not own RuntimeGate's execution lifecycle. Its HTTP mode is a custom JSON POST bridge, not full Streamable HTTP. Claude Code and Cursor native hooks have tested config/event fixtures but unverified native hosts. Codex CLI overrides and MCP SDK calls are tested; project discovery and native invocation are unverified.

ACB is not an OS sandbox, arbitrary-agent containment system, distributed coordinator, or guarantee of exactly-once external effects. Direct tool/subprocess calls that bypass ACB are outside scope. Local HMAC logs are not immutable storage; protect keys and retain rollback-detection checkpoints independently. Readiness checks cannot prove application-wide mediation.

## Website examples

The browser replays policy and approval results recorded from v1.7.2 on November 11. Owner panels quote the published v1.7.2 MinIO report. The video remains a historical v1.7.0 recording, not an owner-service demo. Browser interactions do not execute commands or run Python.
- git push --force origin main: BLOCK.
- DROP TABLE users: BLOCK.
- ls /home: UNKNOWN.
- Synthetic safe-write approval scenario: pending request does not execute; exact approval executes; replay does not execute. This scenario uses the validator's custom evaluator and constrained executor, not a claim that arbitrary writes pass default policy.

## Published validation

The November 9 v1.7.2 release records 723 regression tests plus 444 subtests, 133 legacy live checks, 37 MinIO observed-effect checks and 8 separate-UID Linux isolation checks. TestPyPI and PyPI downloads matched authoritative hashes and executed fresh installed workflows; the published verification records the successful release workflow. This is finite synthetic acceptance coverage, not certification or a universal detector benchmark. Local macOS regression results, MinIO checks, and Linux isolation have separate documented scopes.
